Hazeroth
haz-eh-ROTH
proper noun
Hebrew chatseroth, “enclosures” or “settlements,” a station of Israel where Miriam was struck with leprosy for speaking against Moses.

Biblical Definition

Hazeroth was a station of Israel in the wilderness whither the people journeyed from Kibroth-hattaavah and abode there, and it was here that Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married (Num 11:35; Num 12:1; Num 33:17). They said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? and the LORD heard it. He came down in the pillar of the cloud and rebuked them, declaring that with His servant Moses He spake mouth to mouth, and His anger was kindled, and when the cloud departed, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Moses cried unto the LORD, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee, and she was shut out of the camp seven days, and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again. The dictionary marks Hazeroth not as a contested matter, but as a real camp where the Spirit of God set down a grave warning against the sin of envying the LORD’s appointed servant. Hazeroth stands as a witness that the LORD defends His own anointed and resents the murmuring tongue, yet hears the cry of intercession and is full of mercy; for He struck Miriam in justice but healed her at the prayer of meek Moses, and so taught Israel to fear His honour and to seek His grace.

Webster 1828 Definition

A station of Israel where Miriam was struck with leprosy for speaking against Moses.

HAZEROTH, a station of Israel in the wilderness, signifying “enclosures” or “settlements.”

Israel journeyed thither from Kibroth-hattaavah and abode there.

Here Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses, and the LORD heard it.

Miriam was struck leprous and shut out of the camp seven days.

It witnesses to the LORD’s defence of His servant and His mercy in healing.

Key Scripture

Num 11:35 — "And the people journeyed from Kibroth-hattaavah unto Hazeroth; and abode at Hazeroth."

Num 12:1 — "And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman."

Num 12:10 — "And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous."

Psa 16:6 — "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s defence of His servant and His mercy in healing.

expand to see more

Hazeroth is a real camp of the sacred record, the place where Miriam was struck for her murmuring, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name among the journeys of Israel may know it for a real station in a real pilgrimage, where a real God both chastened and healed.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the LORD’s defence of His appointed servant and His mercy toward the penitent. He who smote Miriam with leprosy for her envious tongue is the same who healed her at the cry of meek Moses. The saint tempted to murmur against those the LORD hath set over him may remember Hazeroth, and learn both to fear God’s honour and to seek His grace, for the lines are fallen in pleasant places to the lowly and not to the proud of tongue.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “enclosures,” Hazeroth names the station where Miriam was struck with leprosy.

Hazeroth — Hebrew chatseroth, “enclosures” or “settlements.”

It was a station of Israel after Kibroth-hattaavah.

Here Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses.

Miriam was struck leprous and shut out of the camp seven days.

The people journeyed not until Miriam was brought in again.

Usage

"Like Israel halted at Hazeroth, the people of God are taught to honour those the LORD hath appointed over them."

"The God who chastened Miriam’s murmuring tongue yet healed her at the intercession of meek Moses."

"He defends His servants in justice and answers prayer in mercy, that His people may fear and trust Him."
